facts.claim: Hinton, Vinyals and Dean train a small model on the class probabilities a large model produces, used as “soft targets”, raising the temperature of the large model’s final softmax until those targets are suitably soft.
The same paper notes that when the soft targets have high entropy, they give much more information per training case than the single right answer does.
FrugalGPT is an LLM cascade that learns which combinations of models to use for different queries; its authors report it can match the best single model (GPT-4) with up to 98% cost reduction.
RouteLLM trains routers that pick between a stronger and a weaker model for each query; its authors report cutting costs by more than half in some cases without losing response quality.
Anthropic lists Claude Haiku 4.5 at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, and Claude Opus 4.5 at $5 and $25: the smaller model costs a fifth as much per token, in and out.
